name: Chips
statusNote: Corner-morphing container shapes, and the springs driving them, are new in Expressive and opt-in for filter and input chips only; the flat/elevated color and elevation model otherwise carries over unchanged from M3.
summary: Compact, tappable elements for input, attributes, filtering, or one-off actions. Use assist for a single contextual action, filter for toggling membership in a content set, input for user-entered discrete values, and suggestion for tapping a dynamically generated hint.

inputs.name: type
inputs.description: Which chip this is; selects selectability, anatomy, and the comp.<type>-chip token group.

inputs.name: onClick
inputs.description: Runs the chip's action (assist, suggestion), or is expected to flip selected (filter, input) — Compose leaves toggling the caller's responsibility.

inputs.name: selected
inputs.description: Selection state for filter and input chips, mirrored into checkbox semantics. Has no effect on assist or suggestion chips, which are plain buttons.

inputs.name: enabled
inputs.description: Disables interaction and shows the disabled colors/opacities.

inputs.name: leadingIcon
inputs.description: Optional icon before the label. On filter/input chips, the caller must swap this for a check glyph when selected is true — Compose does not draw a checkmark itself (Chip.kt:610-612,705-707).

inputs.name: avatar
inputs.description: Input chip only. Takes precedence over leadingIcon when both are supplied — the icon is then discarded, never shown alongside (Chip.kt:1259-1260).

inputs.name: trailingIcon
inputs.description: Decorative on filter chips; the remove/close affordance on input chips (give it its own hit area and label, see accessibility). Not available on suggestion chips, which expose no trailing slot at all.

inputs.name: shapeMorph
inputs.description: Opts into the Expressive corner-morphing ChipShapes API. Filter and input chips only (@material3expressive) — assist and suggestion never morph; no ChipShapes overload exists for them.

inputs.name: style
inputs.description: Elevation/color model. Elevated exists for assist, filter, and suggestion (Elevated*Chip); input chips have one flat elevation level only — there is no ElevatedInputChip in Compose.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: Rounded-rectangle surface. Its corner radius can morph per interaction state instead of using one static shape, when shapeMorph is set (filter/input only).

anatomy.name: Leading icon
anatomy.description: Icon before the label; not shown when an avatar takes its place (input chip).

anatomy.name: Avatar
anatomy.description: A shaped image, input chip only, shown instead of a leading icon when both are supplied.

anatomy.name: Trailing icon
anatomy.description: Decorative on filter chips, the remove/close affordance on input chips; absent from suggestion chips entirely.

anatomy.name: Focus indicator
anatomy.description: A focus ring drawn around the chip. Tokens exist per variant and shared, but Chip.kt implements no focus-indicator paint step at this SHA (see notes).

variants.description: One tap for a smart or contextual action; not selectable (role=button).
Toggle inclusion in a filtered set; selectable (role=checkbox).
Discrete user-entered data; selectable and removable via trailingIcon.
Tap a generated suggestion; not selectable, minimal decoration — the only variant with no trailing-icon slot.
Rests at comp.chips.container-elevation (level0); flat filter chips still define distinct hover/focus/pressed elevation deltas even though resting elevation is 0.
Raises resting elevation via the variant's own elevated-container-elevation/-color tokens. Not available for input chips (no ElevatedInputChip).

One static shape from comp.<type>-chip.container-shape — a different corner value than the morph API's resting comp.chips.unselected-shape; not a conflict, just two separate code paths with two separate defaults.

Opt-in Expressive API, filter and input chips only: corner radius animates between comp.chips.unselected-shape (rest), selected-shape (selected), and pressed-shape (pressed, which wins over selected). See behaviour for the animation mechanics.

layout.text: Content is capped at a 1000dp internal max width. This is an animation-correctness guard for Row-based layout, not a design limit.
Assist and suggestion chips use symmetric content padding regardless of which icon slots are populated.
Filter chips use a default gap between elements, shrunk to a compact gap on whichever side has an icon.
Input chips use asymmetric content padding: start is 4dp if an avatar is present or there is no leading icon, else 8dp; end is 8dp if a trailing icon is present, else 4dp.
The default gap between a chip's own elements (icon/avatar to label to trailing icon) is 8dp and is not tokenized.

Chip.kt has no group/wrap layout of its own. MDC's ChipGroup wraps chips across rows by default, can be forced to one scrolling row, and defaults chip-to-chip spacing to 8dp; resolved tokens carry no group-spacing value, so the kit must supply an equivalent gap itself.

states.text: The selection checkmark is not drawn by Compose: the leadingIcon slot itself is expected to be swapped by the caller for a check glyph. MDC's widget supplies this itself as a checkedIcon overlay, defaulting to a checkmark and visible by default on input and filter chips only.
Border width animates with selection: the unselected outline width drops to the selected outline width (0, coinciding with the container switching to a filled/tonal color) when selected.
In the corner-morphing API, pressed wins over selected: the container takes pressed-shape even while selected.

Flat chips still define distinct hover elevation deltas even though resting elevation is 0; implement as a hover elevation bump on an otherwise flat surface, not a resting shadow. Hover has no effect on label/icon/border color at this SHA (see notes).

Dragging raises the container to its dragged-container-elevation. This is the one dragged-* token per variant that Compose actually reads; the matching dragged-*-color tokens for label/icon are never read (see notes).

Label, leading-icon, and trailing-icon colors dim to the variant's disabled-*-opacity. The input-chip avatar dims separately, to comp.input-chip.disabled-avatar-opacity, rather than sharing the plain leading-icon's disabled opacity.

behaviour.text: Leading/trailing content (icon, avatar, or the selection checkmark) animates in/out whenever it flips between null and non-null, via expand/shrink-horizontally-from-the-relevant-edge plus a fade. On the flat (non-morph) filter/input API this is fast-spatial expand, default-effects shrink, slow-effects fade-in, fast-effects fade-out; the corner-morphing overload instead uses fast-spatial for both expand and shrink and default-effects for both fades (the source marks this timing provisional). While content fades out, the last non-null composable is retained on screen so it animates away instead of disappearing instantly.
Shape morph only animates when unselected-shape, selected-shape, and pressed-shape all share one corner-based shape family; otherwise the container hard-swaps between them with no animation.
No dedicated removal animation exists beyond the trailing-icon shrink/fade above; deleting an input chip from a list is not itself animated by Chip.kt. Animate the list operation yourself.

accessibility.role: button (assist, suggestion); checkbox (filter, input), checked mirroring selected
keyboard: Tab moves focus to the chip.
Enter or Space activates a button-role chip (assist, suggestion) or toggles a checkbox-role chip's selected state (filter, input).

The input chip's trailing remove control needs its own focusable, keyboard-activatable target distinct from the chip body; Chip.kt exposes it only as a bare composable slot with no built-in keyboard affordance.
semantics: Assist and suggestion chips expose button semantics.
Filter and input chips expose checkbox semantics; checked mirrors selected.
Chip label text reaches screen readers automatically; MDC notes that extra content labels are usually unnecessary for it.
The input chip's remove/close control needs its own content description (MDC defaults it to a localized "Close"); Chip.kt supplies neither a hit area nor a label for it, so the kit must add both.

notes.text: At this SHA, comp.chips's own copies of every per-property token are unread except unselected-leading-icon-color and the three morph shapes (unselected-shape, selected-shape, pressed-shape) — the only members of ChipsTokens that Chip.kt actually references. Every other comp.chips token (height, avatar-size, avatar-shape, leading-icon-size, trailing-icon-size, label-text, container-elevation, dragged-container-elevation, focused-indicator-color, the disabled-* and selected-*/unselected-* content and outline colors, selected-outline-width, unselected-outline-width) is always re-sourced from the matching comp.<type>-chip token instead, even when the values would be identical. Despite the .md's framing of comp.chips as the shared source of truth, read the variant group first for anything other than the four live tokens listed here.

ChipColors and SelectableChipColors branch only on (enabled) or (enabled, selected) — a source TODO (b/113855296) explicitly admits hover/focus/drag states aren't supported yet for content color. Every hover-, focus-, pressed-, and dragged- label/icon color token, plus every selected-hover-/selected-focus-/selected-pressed-/selected-dragged- and unselected- counterpart on filter-chip and input-chip, plus every flat-*-focus-outline-color, is unread. Only elevation genuinely branches on interaction (ChipElevation/SelectableChipElevation do read hover/focus/pressed/dragged deltas) — don't assume the same is true of color.

Chip.kt exposes each variant's own single/leading icon size (AssistChipDefaults.IconSize, FilterChipDefaults.IconSize, InputChipDefaults.IconSize, SuggestionChipDefaults.IconSize) as an advisory public constant for callers to size their own icon composable with; the chip never measures or clips the icon slot itself. No TrailingIconSize constant is exposed anywhere in Chip.kt, and neither comp.chips.trailing-icon-size nor comp.input-chip.trailing-icon-size is referenced — size the trailing icon to match the leading one by convention if the design calls for parity.

Suggestion chip's API has no trailing-icon slot at all — only one optional leading icon parameter — making it the minimal-decoration variant. The other three variants all expose both leading and trailing slots.

MDC's minimum touch target is 48dp, auto-extended around the visual container via an inset rather than by resizing it (ensureAccessibleTouchTarget, default on). Chip.kt has no equivalent inset, so this platform-widget behaviour must be replicated deliberately, not read off the token set.

The input-chip trailing/close icon is a bare composable slot in Chip.kt: no built-in minimum hit area and no content description. MDC's widget defaults the close icon's description to a localized "Close" string; the kit must supply both a hit-area and a label for the remove control itself.

The corner-radius interpolation driving shape morph has no named spring in the pinned source beyond the fast-spatial/default-effects pair used for the simultaneous content-swap expand/shrink; treat the shape tween itself as using the same default-effects family unless the design calls for something else.
